content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"It addresses a pressed-link collision between the defender's and challenger's chains over Acts 2:30, so K-C governs how that collision is weighed.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': I weighed reading it as requiring assessment of the competing chains' exhibited support versus reading it as permitting an underdetermination finding from the silence of Acts 2:30 alone.","why":"Because the judge text makes the absence of an explicit body-channel in Acts 2:30 alone decisive for an UNDERDETERMINED finding, it uses the verse-level stating/silence test that K-C retires instead of weighing the chains by footing."}
